- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to align with true mean reversion.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast peak.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true prices often dip 1–3 days after model peaks; shift forecast downward by 1–2% for days 1–3 post-peak.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply a “trend decay” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per 3-day cycle.
- When sentiment is high but price declines sharply, model overreacts; cap forecast decline at 5% below recent high to avoid “sell-off overcorrection.”
